Heard Sri B.Anwar Basha, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara,
learned HCGP for the respondent - State.

2. The petitioner is the accused No.1 in Crime No.118/2023 of Women Police Station, Ballari,
wherein the respondent/police have registered a case for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 306 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
3.

Brief facts of the case:
It is the case of the prosecution that the father of the deceased has lodged a complaint stating that he has performed the marriage of his second daughter with the petitioner herein on 27.04.2019.
The couple had a child by name Girish.
The deceased was taken care nicely by the husband and in laws for eight months.
Thereafter, they started ill-treating and harassing her in one or the other pretext stating that she does not know the household work, cooking etc., and instigated her to commit suicide.

It is stated in the complaint that when the complainant went to the house of the deceased to see the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13317 grandson, the accused No.1 scolded the deceased in front of CW1 and did not allow the complainant to see his child.
4. On 19.07.2023, CW1 has received the message from the relative of accused No.1 that the deceased has committed suicide by hanging herself.
Hence, the complaint came to be registered against the petitioner and others.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case and conducted the investigation and submitted the charge sheet.

5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences, there are some petty issues and quarrels which were being taken place in the family as a matter of routine.
Both the petitioner and the deceased were living happily and also they have begotten a male child.

6. It is further submitted that the complainant has stated in his complaint that he was unnecessarily interfering with the affairs of the family of accused No.1 and there was a rift between CW1 and also the petitioner.
Accused No.1 was not allowing CW1 to go to his house.
Taking advantage on death of the deceased, the complainant has lodged a false NC: 2023:KHC-D:13317 complaint and implicated all the family members of the petitioner herein along with the petitioner.

There were no allegations Mahesha S/O Late Kotrappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156013064/
2 against the petitioner and others in respect of the quarrel and cruelty prior to the suicide.

sentences.text: 7. It is further submitted that there are no grounds to make out a case in respect of abatement to commit suicide.
There were no cases registered nor any panchayaths held in respect of cruelty or harassment.
The complainant intentionally filed a false complaint.
8. The petitioner is the permanent resident of Ward No.31, Karimaramma Colony, Ballari and was working as a coolie and he has to take care of his child and also the aged parents.
He will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

9. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader submitted that the petitioner being the husband of the deceased always used to taunt and harass her on one or the other pretext and it is also established that she had committed suicide on account of cruelty said to have committed by the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13317 petitioner.
The investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.
At this stage, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there may be chances of absconding and fleeing from justice.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.
10. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it appears that the petitioner is the husband of the deceased.
Their marriage was solemnized on 27.04.2019, they have a boy baby, aged about one year.
As per the averments of the complaint, everything was not set in right in the matrimonial house of the deceased.
She was being taunted and being harassed on one or other pretext.
One year ago, she had given birth to a child.
As on the date of the alleged incident, the age of the child was 11 months.

11. Even though the complainant stated in his complaint that the deceased was being subjected to cruelty and harassment at her matrimonial house, no complaints were lodged against the petitioner and others and also no NC: 2023:KHC-D:13317 panchayaths were held with regard to ill-treatment of the deceased.
Even though the deceased committed suicide in the matrimonial home, the nexus between the suicide and the cruelty, as per the averments of the charge sheet, are not sufficiently established.
Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that the petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail.

12. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.118/2023 of Women Police Station, Ballari for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 306 r/w 34 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:-
a) The petitioner shall execute personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
Mahesha S/O Late Kotrappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156013064/
3 b) The petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court regularly without fail.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13317

In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above,
the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
